1.x: John presents Jesus as the Word who became flesh. In this passage, many reject him, but whoever receives him and believes in his name becomes a child of God and receives grace upon grace.
1.f: What changes for you in knowing that God became flesh and dwelt among us?
1.k: The name John gives Jesus in this chapter, the Son who was with God and became flesh.
t: Jesus came to what was his own, but his own did not receive him.
Whoever receives Jesus and believes in his name becomes a child of God.
God's children are born of God, not of human will.
The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
All received from Jesus' fullness, grace upon grace.
Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

5.x: This challenge reviews John, from the Word made flesh to the finished cross. Jesus reveals himself as the way and the vine, and calls the reader to believe in him and remain in him.
5.f: In light of all John has shown, what does believing in Jesus mean to you?
5.k: The name John gives Jesus, the Son who became flesh and dwelt among us.
t: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
Whoever receives Jesus and believes in his name becomes a child of God.
Jesus presents himself as the way, the truth and the life.
Whoever remains in Jesus bears much fruit.
Without Jesus, the disciples can do nothing.
Jesus declares that it is finished and gives up his spirit.

2.x: Jesus is about to leave and comforts the disciples by speaking of the place he will prepare. Thomas and Philip ask questions, and Jesus shows that knowing him is knowing the Father.
2.f: When you don't know which way to go, what changes as you look to Jesus?
2.k: The word with which Jesus presents himself to Thomas, the way to the Father.
t: Jesus will return to receive the disciples to himself.
Thomas says he does not know where Jesus is going.
Jesus presents himself as the way, the truth and the life.
No one comes to the Father except through Jesus.
Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father.
Whoever sees Jesus also sees the Father.

3.x: In his farewell, Jesus compares the disciples' life to branches joined to a vine. Without remaining in him, the branch bears no fruit; joined to him, it bears much fruit and glorifies the Father.
3.f: In what area of your life do you need to stay joined to Jesus today?
3.k: Staying joined to Jesus continually, as the branch remains in the vine.
t: The branch that bears no fruit is cut off, and the one that does is pruned.
The branch cannot bear fruit by itself.
Whoever remains in Jesus bears much fruit.
Without Jesus, the disciples can do nothing.
If Jesus' words remain in them, they will ask and receive.
The Father is glorified when the disciples bear much fruit.

4.x: On the cross, Jesus cares for his mother, says he is thirsty so that Scripture is fulfilled, and declares his work finished. Already dead, his legs are not broken by the soldiers.
4.f: What do you need to entrust to Jesus, believing that his work is complete?
4.k: Jesus' word on the cross as he gave up his life with the work fulfilled.
t: The disciple takes Jesus' mother into his own home.
Jesus says he is thirsty after seeing that all was finished.
They soaked a sponge in sour wine and brought it to Jesus' mouth.
Jesus declares that it is finished and gives up his spirit.
The bodies were not to stay on the cross during the Sabbath.
The soldiers do not break the legs of Jesus, already dead.

1.x: Juan presenta a Jesús como el Verbo que se hizo carne. En este pasaje, muchos lo rechazan, pero quien lo recibe y cree en su nombre llega a ser hijo de Dios y recibe gracia sobre gracia.
1.f: ¿Qué cambia para ti al saber que Dios se hizo carne y habitó entre nosotros?
1.k: Nombre que Juan da a Jesús en este capítulo, el Hijo que estaba con Dios y se hizo carne.
t: Jesús vino a lo suyo, pero los suyos no lo recibieron.
Quien recibe a Jesús y cree en su nombre llega a ser hijo de Dios.
Los hijos de Dios nacen de Dios, y no de la voluntad humana.
El Verbo se hizo carne y habitó entre nosotros.
Todos recibieron de la plenitud de Jesús, gracia sobre gracia.
La gracia y la verdad llegaron por medio de Jesucristo.

5.x: Este desafío repasa Juan, del Verbo hecho carne a la cruz consumada. Jesús se revela como camino y vid, y llama al lector a creer en él y permanecer en él.
5.f: Ante todo lo que Juan mostró, ¿qué significa para ti creer en Jesús?
5.k: Nombre que Juan da a Jesús, el Hijo que se hizo carne y habitó entre nosotros.
t: El Verbo se hizo carne y habitó entre nosotros.
Quien recibe a Jesús y cree en su nombre llega a ser hijo de Dios.
Jesús se presenta como el camino, la verdad y la vida.
Quien permanece en Jesús da mucho fruto.
Sin Jesús, los discípulos nada pueden hacer.
Jesús declara que todo está consumado y entrega el espíritu.

2.x: Jesús está por partir y consuela a los discípulos hablando del lugar que va a preparar. Tomás y Felipe hacen preguntas, y Jesús muestra que conocerlo a él es conocer al Padre.
2.f: Cuando no sabes por dónde ir, ¿qué cambia al mirar a Jesús?
2.k: La palabra con que Jesús se presenta a Tomás, el camino al Padre.
r: Ver a Jesús, ver al Padre
t: Jesús volverá para recibir a los discípulos consigo.
Tomás dice que no sabe adónde va Jesús.
Jesús se presenta como el camino, la verdad y la vida.
Nadie viene al Padre sino por medio de Jesús.
Felipe pide que Jesús les muestre al Padre.
Quien ve a Jesús ve también al Padre.

3.x: En la despedida, Jesús compara la vida de los discípulos con ramas unidas a una vid. Sin permanecer en él, la rama no da fruto; unida a él, da mucho fruto y glorifica al Padre.
3.f: ¿En qué área de tu vida necesitas permanecer unido a Jesús hoy?
3.k: Quedarse unido a Jesús de forma continua, como la rama permanece en la vid.
t: La rama que no da fruto es cortada, y la que da es limpiada.
La rama no puede producir fruto por sí misma.
Quien permanece en Jesús da mucho fruto.
Sin Jesús, los discípulos nada pueden hacer.
Si las palabras de Jesús permanecen en ellos, pedirán y recibirán.
El Padre es glorificado cuando los discípulos dan mucho fruto.

4.x: En la cruz, Jesús cuida de su madre, dice tener sed para que se cumpla la Escritura y declara su obra consumada. Ya muerto, los soldados no le quiebran las piernas.
4.f: ¿Qué necesitas confiarle a Jesús, creyendo que su obra está completa?
4.k: La palabra de Jesús en la cruz, al entregar la vida con la obra cumplida.
t: El discípulo recibe a la madre de Jesús en su propia casa.
Jesús dice tener sed después de ver que todo estaba consumado.
Empaparon una esponja en vinagre y la llevaron a la boca de Jesús.
Jesús declara que todo está consumado y entrega el espíritu.
Los cuerpos no debían quedar en la cruz durante el sábado.
Los soldados no quiebran las piernas de Jesús, ya muerto.
